items.title: A countable discrete measurable space is standard Borel
items.statement: If S is nonempty and at most countable, then (S,P(S)) is standard Borel.
items.strategy: Use the discrete metric: it is complete and induces the power-set Borel sigma-algebra, while S itself is an at most countable dense subset.

references.title: David Marker, Descriptive Set Theory, Example 1.2, course notes (Fall 2002)
references.locator: §1, Example 1.2, PDF p. 2: the discrete metric on a countable set is complete and induces the discrete topology.

items.title: Poisson random measure on a standard Borel space
items.statement: Define a Poisson random measure on a standard Borel space with sigma-finite intensity through its measurable counting-measure evaluations and independent finite-intensity Poisson counts.
items.strategy: State the measurable evaluation convention for countably additive counting measures and the finite-intensity independent-count property.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in the definition.

references.title: Günter Last and Mathew Penrose, Lectures on the Poisson Process, 2017, Chapter 3
Thomas S. Ferguson, A Bayesian Analysis of Some Nonparametric Problems, 1973

items.title: Dirichlet process
items.statement: Define DP(alpha) as the probability law on evaluation-measurable probability measures whose masses on each finite measurable partition have the Dirichlet law after omitting zero-base cells.
items.strategy: Specify the evaluation sigma-algebra, finite nonzero base-measure regime, positive-cell Dirichlet law, and deterministic zero-base cells.
items.axiom_use: Dirichlet density normalization inherits Countable Choice from the declared BCS-03 definition.

references.title: Thomas S. Ferguson, A Bayesian Analysis of Some Nonparametric Problems, 1973, Section 3
Subhashis Ghosal and Aad van der Vaart, Posterior convergence rates of Dirichlet mixtures at smooth densities, 2007

items.title: Existence of a Dirichlet process by normalized gamma Poisson random measure
items.statement: Under AC, construct a measurable countably additive random probability measure by normalizing a Poisson random measure with intensity alpha(dx)t^(-1)e^(-t)dt; its finite partition increments are independent Gamma(alpha(A_j),1) variables before normalization and its masses have the required Dirichlet laws.
items.strategy: Partition the gamma mark axis into finite-intensity strips, construct independent Poisson counts and marks by countable standard-Borel product laws, prove the Poisson random-measure count laws, compute gamma increments by their exponential transforms, and normalize them.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is used for the countable standard-Borel product construction through Kolmogorov extension; AC implies the Countable Choice required by the gamma and Dirichlet normalizations.

references.title: Günter Last and Mathew Penrose, Lectures on the Poisson Process, 2017, Chapters 1 and 3
Thomas S. Ferguson, A Bayesian Analysis of Some Nonparametric Problems, 1973, Sections 2 and 3

items.title: Dirichlet parameters add under coarsening
items.statement: For a positive-parameter Dirichlet vector, summing coordinates over a partition of the index set gives a Dirichlet vector whose parameters are the corresponding sums.
items.strategy: Represent the positive Dirichlet vector by normalized independent shape-rate Gamma variables, identify sums over disjoint groups by their moment-generating functions, and normalize the grouped variables.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is inherited through the normalized-gamma construction and the exponential-transform uniqueness lemma; no stronger choice principle is used.

references.title: Thomas S. Ferguson, A Bayesian Analysis of Some Nonparametric Problems, 1973, Section 2
Günter Last and Mathew Penrose, Lectures on the Poisson Process, 2017, Chapter 1

items.title: Dirichlet-process posterior update
items.statement: Under AC and conditionally IID sampling from G~DP(alpha), a measurable posterior kernel version is DP(alpha+sum_i delta_xi); the statement includes supported fibers and specifies the formula as only a version on prior-predictive null fibers.
items.strategy: Prove measurability of the updated Dirichlet-process law on finite-partition cylinders, verify the posterior disintegration identity on common refinements using the finite-dimensional Dirichlet-multinomial update, then extend both identities by pi-lambda uniqueness.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is carried from the normalized-gamma existence theorem and supplies the Countable Choice assumed by the finite-dimensional Dirichlet update.

references.title: Thomas S. Ferguson, A Bayesian Analysis of Some Nonparametric Problems, 1973, Sections 2 and 3
Subhashis Ghosal and Aad van der Vaart, Posterior convergence rates of Dirichlet mixtures at smooth densities, 2007

items.title: Dirichlet-process Pólya-urn predictive law
items.statement: Under the posterior version DP(alpha+sum_i delta_xi), the next-draw predictive probability of a measurable set A is (alpha(A)+sum_i 1_A(x_i))/(alpha(X)+n), including zero-base and one-cell boundaries.
items.strategy: Take the posterior expectation of G(A); obtain the one-cell predictive probability from the Dirichlet-multinomial update and handle zero-parameter cells by their deterministic mass.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is inherited through the posterior and normalized-gamma theorems and implies the Countable Choice used in Dirichlet conjugacy.

references.title: Thomas S. Ferguson, A Bayesian Analysis of Some Nonparametric Problems, 1973, Sections 2 and 3
Günter Last and Mathew Penrose, Lectures on the Poisson Process, 2017, Chapter 1

items.title: Finite-partition conjugacy gives no density-contraction theorem
items.statement:
The normalized-gamma construction and finite-partition posterior update
state no topology on $\mathcal P(\mathsf X)$ and specify no density model.
They therefore establish neither a weak-support theorem nor density-posterior
consistency or contraction. A weak-support claim requires a specified topology
and an argument that the prior assigns positive mass to each neighborhood in
question. A density-posterior consistency or contraction claim additionally
requires a specified sampling model and truth class, plus its own proof under
the relevant model-specific hypotheses. For example, the finite-dimensional
prior-mass bound in Ghosal--van der Vaart is one ingredient in a separate
mixture analysis, not a consequence of the conjugate update alone.
items.strategy: State the precise boundary of the finite-partition existence and update results without asserting a topology-dependent support or contraction theorem.
items.axiom_use: The referenced Dirichlet-process results assume full AC.

references.title: Subhashis Ghosal and Aad van der Vaart, Posterior convergence rates of Dirichlet mixtures at smooth densities, 2007, Section 7
Thomas S. Ferguson, A Bayesian Analysis of Some Nonparametric Problems, 1973, Section 3

title: Dirichlet-process priors and finite-partition updates — Examples

items.title: Finite-partition posterior and Pólya-urn draws
items.statement: For a three-point space with Dirichlet base masses (2,1,1), verify the posterior after observations a,b and the exact next-draw probabilities, including reinforcement after one draw of a.
items.strategy: Update the three Dirichlet parameters by the cell counts and evaluate the predictive formula for the first and second draws.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is inherited from the normalized-gamma construction and posterior result.

references.title: Thomas S. Ferguson, A Bayesian Analysis of Some Nonparametric Problems, 1973, Sections 2 and 3
Günter Last and Mathew Penrose, Lectures on the Poisson Process, 2017, Chapter 1

items.title: A base-null observation is a prior-predictive null fiber
items.statement: On a two-point space with base measure supported at a, the event that an IID observation equals b has prior-predictive probability zero; the DP update formula at b is one valid kernel value and may be changed on that null data set.
items.strategy: Use the zero-base-cell law to show the event is null, then change the posterior kernel on its measurable null fiber and check the disintegration identity is unchanged.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is inherited from the normalized-gamma and posterior results.

references.title: Thomas S. Ferguson, A Bayesian Analysis of Some Nonparametric Problems, 1973, Section 3
Subhashis Ghosal and Aad van der Vaart, Posterior convergence rates of Dirichlet mixtures at smooth densities, 2007, Section 7
